Rise and Grind
RYZ und GRYND
phrase (Millennial slang)
A 2010s variation of the old wake-up call rise and shine (itself early twentieth-century, often military). Rise and grind spread through fitness and entrepreneurial social media as a morning mantra of hustle culture: get up early, work harder than everyone else, never stop. It appeared on gym walls, coffee mugs, and countless Instagram captions at 5 a.m.; the investor Daymond John used it as the title of a 2018 book. Gen Z later mocked it alongside "hustle porn."

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Rise and grind is the hustle-culture alarm clock: up before dawn, straight to work or the gym, outwork everyone, rest when you are dead. It is posted as a badge of discipline and ambition. The Christian observation: half of this is wisdom and half is idolatry, and the halves need separating. Scripture loves early rising and hard work. The sluggard is mocked for loving his bed: "How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?" (Pro 6:9). The virtuous woman "riseth also while it is yet night" (Pro 31:15). The Lord Jesus Himself, "rising up a great while before day," went out to pray (Mar 1:35). Note what He did with the early hour: He prayed before He worked. But Scripture also contains a sentence that reads like a rebuke written for this slogan: "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep" (Psa 127:2). The grind that never stops, that measures a man’s worth by hours and output, that treats sleep and Sabbath as weakness, is labour without the Lord, and "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it" (Psa 127:1). A father teaches his son to get up early, to work hard, and to begin the day with God; and to know that he is not what he produces, that rest is commanded, and that the Lord gives to His beloved even in their sleep.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial hustle-culture mantra (2010s; from rise and shine) for early rising and relentless work; diligence and early prayer are biblical (Pro 6:9; Mar 1:35), but labour without the Lord and without rest is vain (Psa 127:1-2).

RISE AND GRIND, phr. (Millennial hustle-culture slang, 2010s) A morning motto urging early rising and relentless work or training. Related: hustle culture, grindset, "team no sleep."

Webster (1828), root grind: GRIND, verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive ground. [This word, if n is radical, may be allied to rend; if not, it coincides with grate; to make smooth, as mollis in Latin , allied to molo.] 1. To break and reduce to fine particles or powder by friction; to comminute by attrition; to triturate. Take the millstones and grind meal. Isaiah 47:2 . We say, to grind meal, but this is an elliptical phrase. The true phrase is, to grind corn to meal. 2. To break and reduce to small pieces by the teeth. 3. […]

Decode for parents: teach the early hour and the hard day, and teach that worth is not output and rest is commanded.

Key Scripture

Pro 6:9 — "How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?"

Pro 31:15 — "She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens."

Mar 1:35 — "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed."

Psa 127:2 — "It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep."

Psa 127:1 — "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain."

Modern Corruption

Rise and grind joins true diligence to the idolatry of endless work; Scripture praises the early riser who prays first and calls the sleepless grind without the Lord vain.

expand to see more

The corruption is work as identity and salvation. The grind mindset promises that enough effort will produce worth, wealth, and meaning, and it treats rest as failure. That is the treadmill of Babel, building a name by labour. Scripture’s word for it is vanity: rising early and sitting up late without the Lord produces bread of sorrows. The grind also tends to crowd out prayer, family, and the Lord’s Day, the very things that make work meaningful.

The recovery is diligence under grace. Christians should be the hardest workers in any room, not to earn their worth but because they already have it. Begin the day with God, as Jesus did; work heartily as to the Lord; stop at evening; keep the Sabbath; and sleep well, trusting Him. Teach the young that discipline is a fruit of the Spirit, not a brand, and that the Lord who neither slumbers nor sleeps lets His people do both.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English grindan (to crush) → grind (hard, monotonous work) → "rise and shine" → 2010s hustle-culture rise and grind.

expand to see more

Old English grindan — to rub, to crush small

19th c.: the grind — hard, monotonous work or study

Early 20th c.: "rise and shine"; 2010s: rise and grind on gym walls and Instagram

2018: Daymond John, Rise and Grind; later Gen Z "hustle porn" mockery

Biblical anchor: rising up a great while before day … and there prayed (Mar 1:35); so he giveth his beloved sleep (Psa 127:2)
